outcomes: A CI job that is not Putnami's uploads its change evidence document to Putnami Cloud with a workspace token, or a person uploads it after signing in, and the run shows its tests, coverage, components, changed-line coverage and dependency changes, marked as self-reported, at the report URL the upload answers
nonGoals: Creating the observed workspace or its token: the runbook does it by hand for this slice
Keying the repository of a CI that names no numeric project id: a document without one is refused

requirements.text: putnami cloud evidence-report --file <path> reads a protocol/evidence v1 document and opens its run with POST /v1/delivery/records under the PUTNAMI_CLOUD_TOKEN bearer: the subject's provider, numeric project id as repo, commit and branch, the provenance of the CI, the pull or merge request as changeRequest, conclusion failure when a test failed, else success, and a submission id derived from the CI job, so a repeated upload opens no second run.

text: The provenance is gha for a github-actions document, gitlab for a gitlab-ci one and external for any other CI it names.
A generic document is external when the environment of the upload is a CI by the evidence protocol's markers, and local otherwise.

The run carries under operational what the job tested, read with Git where the command was invoked: testedTree when the subject's commit is the merge the CI built (GitHub refs/pull/<n>/merge at GITHUB_SHA, a GitLab merged results or merge train pipeline at CI_COMMIT_SHA), else testedHeadTree;
with it, baselineMergeBase of the document's base and commit.
A value Git cannot compute is left out with a warning naming it and why.
A run refused for its operational opens again without it.

After the run, it posts the tests and coverage of each component in one batch to POST /v1/delivery/records/reports, then the components, the changed-line coverage and the dependency changes, copied from the document, in a second batch under the same submission id.
A batch with nothing to carry is not sent.

Each dependency change in the second batch keeps the before and after states the document gives it: the licenses and the known vulnerabilities, each with its id and severity, and an empty state as empty.
A dependency change without a state uploads the same body as before the states existed.
A batch refused with 413 for its size while it carries states is posted again without them, with a warning that names the refusal.

Without PUTNAMI_CLOUD_TOKEN, with a document that does not parse or validate, or with a document whose subject names no numeric project id, it sends nothing and exits non-zero with a message that names the cause.
A refused run or batch exits non-zero with the route and the server's reason, and never prints the token;
a run opened again without its operational counts as refused only when that call is refused too.
Under --output=json a refused batch prints one failure result naming the run and what it stored.

With --sign-in and no PUTNAMI_CLOUD_TOKEN, the command uses the session putnami cloud login stored, refreshed when it expired, and runs the same device sign-in when none exists, then uploads as that person: the run names the repository and no workspace, and Putnami Cloud opens the observed workspace in the person's organization.
With a token in PUTNAMI_CLOUD_TOKEN, the upload names the repository too: an organization's ingest token needs it.
Without --sign-in and without a token, it refuses as before.

requirements.text: The result carries data.reportUrl, the report URL Delivery answers when it opens the run, when that is an absolute https URL, and the summary line names it.
